questions.question: Describe the layout of a tender budget sheet and explain the rounding rule with two examples.
questions.expected_answer: The sheet heads with project, team, date and price validity, then sections: Materials with one line per item showing quantity, unit, unit price, source and total; Labour with trades, workers, days, daily rate and total; Transport with each delivery or trip; Allowances of 10 percent of materials for waste and 10 percent of the subtotal for contingency; then the Total and a note of exclusions. Quantities are rounded up to the units actually sold or hired, so 22.4 bags of cement becomes 23 and 19 metres of tube becomes four 6 metre lengths, 24 metres, because rounding down understates what will be paid.

questions.question: Using the working drawing, list the main material quantities for the stairs and ramp and the labour and transport lines you would include.
questions.expected_answer: Concrete: ramp slab about 1.3 cubic metres, landing 0.27, stairs and foundation about 0.6, kerb about 0.11, total about 2.3, needing about 17 bags of cement, 1.5 cubic metres each of sand and stone as sold; hardcore fill about 2.6 cubic metres by the load; two sheets of mesh; shuttering planks and pegs; about 19 metres of handrail and 14 metres of post tube, 33 metres of galvanised tube or a fabricator's quote for rails supplied and fitted; 16 anchor bolts; a rubber movement strip. Labour: one bricklayer and two general workers for 8 days plus a rail installer for 1 day, at local daily rates. Transport: hardcore delivery, two merchant deliveries, the fabricator's delivery, and crew travel.

questions.question: Explain the three checks applied to the budget total and distinguish legitimate savings from illegitimate ones.
questions.expected_answer: Arithmetic: a second person re-multiplies every line and re-adds the columns. Sense: the total is compared with what similar entrances cost in the week 4 analysis or a builder's rule of thumb, and a large difference means a slipped decimal or unit to be found. Proportion: materials, labour and transport as percentages of the total, with materials usually the largest share for concrete work. Legitimate savings keep every specification: a straight ramp if it fits the site, site-mixed instead of ready-mixed concrete, fabricated rails instead of welding on site, local hardcore. Illegitimate: shortening the ramp beyond 1 in 12, cutting the waste or contingency allowances, rounding down or leaving out transport.
